page.layout: One block of running text in a single column, with a woodcut historiated initial "A" at the start; a decorative woodcut border at the top above the text. No margin notes, no running head, no page number printed.

main_text.p: ANalyticam Expositionem Epistolarum Apostolicarum a Cl: viro Domino Davide Dicsono concinnatam, legi avidus; guftatâ antea suavissimâ necnon ut ilissimâ ejus commentatione Anglico jdiomate, in Epistolam ad Hebræos, conscriptâ; De utrâq; dicam quod sentio, jmo quod res est, Satis multum in jis reperturum, qui non expectat nimis. Nec quicquam me vidisse in tanta brevitate, tantum porrigens, et sensus genuini sacri textus et fructus jnde colligendi. Gratulor itaq; Jnsulanis nostris præsertim studiosæ juventuti, tam egregia Doctrinæ, quæ est secundum pietatem, adminicula. Multum a R. Authore efflagitans, tam ut utramque curet (quod de postremâ hâc videtur promittere) & doctis & Jdiotis communicarj; quam ut denuò se accingat ad enarrandas

page.notes: The initial "A" is a large woodcut initial; it is transcribed as "A" joined to "Nalyticam" with the first letter read as A. Printing irregularities (e.g. "Dicsono", "jdiomate", "ilissimâ") are left as printed. The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page with "enarrandas", a catchword-like line set right-aligned, which is treated as the last line of the text.
